newsitem.title: SPAIN: BASKETBALL-FAVOURITES YUGOSLAVIA BEATEN BY ITALY.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-FAVOURITES YUGOSLAVIA BEATEN BY ITALY.

text.p: Italy caused the first big upset of the European men's basketball championships on Thursday by beating favourites Yugoslavia 74-69.
The fancied Croatian side went down 78-71 to Spain.
Both Italy and Spain guaranteed themselves places in the second phase, while Lithuania and Greece will also go through after beating France and Russia respectively.
Neither Croatia nor Yugoslavia are likely to miss out on the next round, as only the bottom team from each group will be eliminated.
Italy went in at the break 42-35 up, and extended their lead in the second half before allowing Yugoslavia to fight back in a frantic final five minutes.
Carlton Myers top scored for the Italians with 23 points.
Another naturalised American, Mike Smith, was also in fine form as Spain turned round a four-point deficit at the break.
The key to the home side's victory was a tactical adjustment which cut out the Croats' three-pointers.
Spanish coach Lolo Sanz was ecstatic after the game.
"For the first time in many years, the team played as a team and not like a group of squabbling families," said Sanz.
Boosted by Wednesday's comfortable win over Turkey, Greece started strongly to build up a commanding 39-21 lead against Russia.
But consecutive three-pointers from Igor Koudelin enabled the Russians to go in at the break only 10 points adrift, and in the end the Greeks struggled to take the game 74-72.
Lithuania were once again led by Arturas Karnisovas in the 94-88 win over France. Karnisovas scored 31 points and was backed up by centre Einikis Gintaras, who scored 27.

Ukraine, Poland, Bosnia and Slovenia are all facing early exits from the competition having lost both their opening games. Ukraine were beaten 81-60 by Germany, Bosnia lost 70-62 to Turkey, and Latvia went down 79-86 to Poland.
Slovenia led their game with Israel from the start, but lost 69-68 in the tournament's closest match so far after giving up a foul with just four seconds on the clock.
